section.title: Cool Down (5 minutes)
Student Activity
section.para: Function \(Q\) gives a puppy’s weight, in pounds, as a function of its age, in months.

list.item:
What does each expression or equation represent in this situation?
\(Q(18)\)
\(Q(30)=27.5\)

section.para:
Answer:
A. the weight of the puppy when it was 18 months old
B. When the puppy was 30 months old, it weighed 27.5 pounds.

list.item:
Use function notation to represent each statement.
When the puppy turned 12 months old, it weighed 19.6 pounds.
When the puppy was \(m\) months old, it weighed \(w\) pounds.

section.title: Response to Student Thinking
More Chances
section.para: Students will have more opportunities to understand the mathematical ideas in this cool-down, so there is no need to slow down or add additional work to the next lessons. Instead, use the results of this cool-down to provide guidance for what to look for and emphasize over the next several lessons to support students in advancing their current understanding.
